newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan business group to leave for North Korea.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan business group to leave for North Korea.

text.p: A major Taiwanese business group will leave for North Korea on Tuesday to explore business and investment opportunities despite the absence of formal ties, an organiser said on Monday.

The group, comprising of 30 business leaders from small- and medium-sized firms, plans to visit the communist state for one week, Joseph Chen, deputy secretary-general of the Chinese National Federation of Industries, said by telephone.
"North Korea is a completely new market for Taiwan businessmen. We have decided to take a look and see if there are any business or investment opportunities," Chen said.

Taiwanese businesses have shown increasing interest in North Korea after they poured millions of dollars into Southeast Asian countries in recent years to avoid surging wages and real estate prices at home.
In April, North Korea set up an authorised tourism office in Taipei to issue "travel certificates", which are equal to visas, for Taiwanese tourists and businessmen.
North Korea maintains full diplomatic ties with China, Taiwan's rival after a Chinese civil war ended in 1949, and has little contact with Taiwan.
South Korea, Pyongyang's enemy, was Taiwan's biggest diplomatic ally in Asia before it switched ties to Beijing in 1992.
Taiwan has angrily suspended air links with Seoul and cancelled trade privileges, hurting tourism in and trade with South Korea.
